## Description
**P1 — A late Session metadata read can roll back the Web cache after a successful revision-guarded save.** This is a distinct post-closure defect relative to [#2789](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/2789) (accepted persistence, revision CAS, editor UX) and [#2970](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/2970) (accepted cross-Session editor-local async completion fencing). Neither acceptance proves ordering between a forced metadata read and a successful write **for the same Session**.

The Agent remains authoritative and its persisted metadata is not shown to be corrupted. The Web cache can nevertheless present a previously fetched revision after the user has just saved a newer one, violating Session-first truthful work context.

## Reproduction
Deterministic source-derived ordering, to be exercised in the existing Session metadata browser/transport fixture:
1. Session S has revision 1 and title "Before". Open Session details and begin editing.
2. Trigger `loadSessionMetadata(S, { force: true })` (for example transport replacement/reconnect) and hold its `sessionsApi.getMetadata` response containing revision 1.
3. Save the edited title "After" with expectedRevision 1. Resolve `sessionsApi.updateMetadata` successfully with revision 2. `saveSessionMetadata` publishes revision 2 and the UI reports success.
4. Resolve the earlier forced read with revision 1. Since `saveSessionMetadata` never advances `requestSequence`, the old read's sequence is still current; `loadSessionMetadata` publishes revision 1, rolling the sidebar title/details back to "Before" despite the successful save.
5. Negative controls: a read that genuinely started *after* the save may publish the latest authoritative revision; failed/conflicted saves must not be treated as successful writes; concurrent Sessions remain independently keyed.

**Verified static proof:** `web/src/product/session/state/metadata.ts` increments and checks `requestSequence` only in `loadSessionMetadata`; `saveSessionMetadata` publishes a successful response without invalidating in-flight reads. The above ordering follows directly from those branches. **Not yet runtime verified:** actual reconnect timing and the rendered browser sequence; frequency in production is unknown.

## Root Cause
Per-Session request ordering only serializes reads against reads. A successful write does not fence an older pending read, so the read's stale response is still eligible to overwrite the cache. Server-side revision CAS cannot prevent this client-side projection regression.

## Impact
A successfully saved Session title/description/tags can temporarily revert in the sidebar and Workspace details; subsequent editing may use the stale displayed revision and produce an avoidable conflict. Users can reasonably believe their work context was not saved, although the Agent's authoritative state is newer.

## Fix Direction
At the metadata cache owner, fence any read started before a successful write (e.g. advance per-Session generation on successful save), and ensure subsequent reads and successful saves preserve revision monotonicity. Do not introduce a second authoritative metadata store, global async framework, tmux rename, or new UI interaction. Preserve conflict draft semantics and the existing #2970 editor identity protection.

## Location
- [web/src/product/session/state/metadata.ts](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/session/state/metadata.ts): `loadSessionMetadata`, `saveSessionMetadata`, `requestSequence`, `publish`.
- [web/src/product/session/hooks/useSessionMetadata.ts](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/session/hooks/useSessionMetadata.ts): reconnect-triggered forced read.
- [web/src/product/session/hooks/useSessionMetadataEditor.ts](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/session/hooks/useSessionMetadataEditor.ts): save completion and edit state.
- [web/src/product/session/components/SessionDetails.tsx](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/session/components/SessionDetails.tsx): user-facing projection.

### Success Criteria
- [ ] SC-01 With a forced metadata read for Session S pending, a successful save of newer revision N followed by the older read's completion never replaces the saved title, description, tags, or revision in the shared Session cache and rendered Session details/navigation.
- [ ] SC-02 Concurrent reads/saves of different Sessions remain isolated; a failed/conflicted save does not falsely advance the displayed authoritative revision, and a subsequent fresh read can still update the cache.

**SC → scenario:** SC-01/02 = SCN-02, existing Chromium + Playwright Session metadata interaction Case with deferred `getMetadata`/`updateMetadata` responses, actual Session details and sidebar DOM assertions, and isolated negative controls. Earliest valid boundary: exact PR head; approved browser Case runner, no credentials or native host requirements. Record source SHA, Case Run/Attempt, action order, rendered title/revision and assertion counts.
